text:
The Blue Jackets snapped a losing skid Thursday in Chicago, and they needed it. That win came after a run where Jet Greaves lost six straight starts and The Hockey News asked whether this was rock bottom. At 8-12-0, Columbus has just 16 points.

The frustrating part is that the chances have been closer than the results. The Jackets have scored about 10.5 fewer goals than their chances deserved, the kind of gap that usually narrows with time, and our numbers say their play earned roughly 19 points, not 16. Still, a 47% share of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against) is not a playoff team's profile.

The summer reshaped the forward group, with Matthew Knies arriving from Toronto and Valeri Nichushkin in the lineup, but the injuries have piled up: Conor Garland went on injured reserve week-to-week and Sean Monahan has been day-to-day with an upper-body injury, which broke up the line the three had formed. The checking trio of Charlie Coyle, Mathieu Olivier and Cole Sillinger has carried the most 5-on-5 minutes and come out ahead on chances. Zach Werenski and Damon Severson have outscored teams 15-8 together.

Our playoff odds give Columbus 7%. What we'd watch: whether Knies, Kent Johnson and Adam Fantilli start turning an even line into a winning one, because the finishing has to come from somewhere.
headline: Columbus is better than 8-12, but not by enough
